This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via expiresAt (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via expiresAt (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via expiresAt (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0a6948210cc96a95cc568b30193895e157968c01` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6da05dff5f34df7e492fbc300073145d957870de` — the merge of head `34331f6613fdcb19e8495de4210887c15bfc0566` into base `0a6948210cc96a95cc568b30193895e157968c01`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6da05dff5f34df7e492fbc300073145d957870de && git checkout 6da05dff5f34df7e492fbc300073145d957870de
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0a6948210cc96a95cc568b30193895e157968c01 34331f6613fdcb19e8495de4210887c15bfc0566 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0a6948210cc96a95cc568b30193895e157968c01 && git merge --no-ff 34331f6613fdcb19e8495de4210887c15bfc0566

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0a6948210cc96a95cc568b30193895e157968c01
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0a6948210cc96a95cc568b30193895e157968c01` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `34331f6613fdcb19e8495de4210887c15bfc0566`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-organization-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-role-label.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-role-label.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/auth-templates-locales.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/builtin-auth-render-identity.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/plain-text-faces.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/templates/auth-templates.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts (resolveAndRenderTemplate, the required-variable check), packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts (requireVars, the formatter call site), packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-loader.ts (the slot rule: any non-built-in item wins, with its own variables), packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-plugin.ts (the built-in rows are code-declared under the email plugin's package), packages/formula/src/template-engine.ts (asDate and the datetime formatter: dateStyle long, timeStyle long, the reference timeZone), packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts (translateMetaList, translationBundleOf), packages/spec/src/system/email-template.zod.ts (the variable type enum already holds `date`; EMAIL_TEMPLATE_FLOOR_LOCALE is `en-US`), packages/spec/src/identity/membership-role.ts (the authored option labels), packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/en, zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES .objects.generated.ts (the sys_member.role option labels per bundle), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs and scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (what the two changeset gates read)

Inputs read: card #25802 (body and all four comments, the claim 6413932028 and the two os-dev-reports 6414584447 and 6415196510 included), PR #26072 (body, file list, net diff against origin/main at this head, and the diff from the previously reviewed head `ee295b9bd00a5093859809fdce2962d4a1f9c893` to this one) and the check-runs on this head as they stood at 2026-10-26T12:30Z. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

This head supersedes the FAIL record on `ee295b9bd00a5093859809fdce2962d4a1f9c893`. The move from that head is one commit, `test(plugin-email): pin the invitation expiry against this Node's Intl, not one ICU release's wording`, and it is test-only: it touches `auth-templates-locales.test.ts`, `builtin-auth-render-identity.test.ts` and `plain-text-faces.test.ts` and nothing else (73 insertions, 30 deletions); the changeset, both plugin-auth source files, the template rows and the plugin-auth test are byte-identical to the reviewed head, and the merge base with `origin/main` is unchanged (`e0fe7d35`). The whole-PR diff against `origin/main` therefore publishes exactly what the earlier record judged, and ① items 1 to 8 and 10 below are restated unchanged; item 9 is re-judged on the patch.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The narrowing, right.** The four built-in `auth.invitation` rows (en-US, zh-CN, ja-JP, es-ES) each declare a new variable `expiresAt`, `type: 'date'`, `required: true`, and every body (HTML and text) ends with one unconditional sentence rendering `{{ expiresAt | datetime:long }}`. `resolveAndRenderTemplate` (email-service.ts 1422-1431) reads `variables_json` off the resolved row and `requireVars` (template-engine.ts 171-179) refuses a send whose data holds no such key with `MISSING_VARIABLES: expiresAt`. So the accept set of `sendTemplate({ template: 'auth.invitation' })` against the built-in rows shrinks: a send that used to be delivered is now refused. Declaring it required is the right choice: the engine has no conditionals (template-engine.ts docblock, line 32: branching belongs in the caller), so an optional variable would ship the dangling sentence the dev measured.
2. **The only in-repo sender, confirmed.** `git grep` at this head over non-test code finds one `template: 'auth.invitation'` send: auth-manager-organization-plugin.ts:624 (the other five `sendTemplate` sites name verify_email, email_change_notice, magic_link, existing_account_sign_up, and service-messaging's email channel passes a caller-supplied name). objectui and hotcrm carry no reference. The built-in sender always passes `expiresAt` when better-auth's `invitation.expiresAt` reads as a date, so the narrowing bites only code outside this repository that sends `auth.invitation` itself, which is exactly what the BREAKING banner names.
3. **An override row escapes the requirement and is not broken by it, right.** `createRegistryEmailTemplateLoader` (template-loader.ts 156-160) resolves one `(name, locale)` slot to any item whose `_packageId` is not the built-in package, and `toRenderInput` (79-94) serialises THAT item's own `variables`. An app or Studio (environment) override of `auth.invitation` therefore keeps its own bodies and its own declared variables: it is not refused for lacking `expiresAt`, and the extra `expiresAt` key the sender now passes is ignored by a body that does not interpolate it. The changeset's sentence on overrides is accurate. One consequence worth knowing: an override that replaces only one locale leaves the other locales on the built-in rows, which do now require the value; the built-in sender supplies it, so nothing breaks.
4. **No stored row is on the path, right.** The loader's module doc (template-loader.ts 3-10) and email-plugin.ts (472-488) say the built-ins are code-declared under `com.objectstack.service.email` and nothing is copied into `sys_email_template` for the send path, so no stored row is read, rewritten or converted by this diff. That is the fact the adr-0087 disposition rests on, and it holds.
5. **Metadata-protocol: none, right.** `EmailTemplateDefinitionVariableSchema` already admits `type: 'date'` (email-template.zod.ts:100); no spec file moves; the diff touches no `packages/spec/**` path, as the claim required.
6. **Nothing widens.** `invitationExpiryArg` and `AUTHORED_LABEL_LANGUAGE` are module-private; plugin-email's `index.ts` exports are unchanged; the new hole is additive output and the two warns are logging. The declared arm is `no (narrowing)` and the diff carries no `yes` fact. The `Clause-②: no (narrowing: ...)` arm is the right one.
7. **The sender's unreadable-expiry path, right with one note.** `invitationExpiryArg` accepts a Date, a string or a number and omits anything that does not parse (`Invalid Date` is never rendered). The omitted value makes the send refused; the existing catch at line 654-659 swallows that refusal with a `console.error`, and the new warn (613-621) names the invitation id and says the mail will be refused, so the operator can resend. Note, not a defect: a numeric epoch in seconds would be read as milliseconds and render a 1970 date; better-auth hands a Date, so the branch is unreachable from the built-in path.
8. **The untranslated-label warn (invitation-role-label.ts 116-132), correct as read.** No false positive on English mails: `isAuthoredLabelLanguage` lowercases, splits on `-` or `_` and compares the language subtag to `en`, so en-US, en-GB and the floor locale (`EMAIL_TEMPLATE_FLOOR_LOCALE` = `en-US`, the value when the send names none) all skip the block. One warn per degradation: the block is guarded by `!readFailed`, so a thrown read keeps its own warn and gets no second one; a token outside the option list fails `labels.has(token)` and stays with its own existing warn; a list of tokens produces one `deps.warn` call naming every untranslated token. The comparison is against the authored labels in `@objectstack/spec/identity` (Owner, Admin, Delegated Admin, Member, External); the `en` bundle carries the same five strings, so an English fallback-chain hit is detected, and the zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES bundles carry no label equal to its English text, so a translated mail never warns. The meta names the role, the locale and whether a service was present. The only false-positive shape is a tenant translation that deliberately equals the English word, which is the mail being in English anyway.
9. **The ICU pin fix is test-only and does not weaken what the pins prove.** The earlier head pinned ICU-rendered wording literally (hand-written expiry sentences per locale, and sha256 digests of faces that contained the `datetime:long` output), which is locale DATA of the running Node, not template text; the dev measured es-ES moving from `2031, 5:06:07` (ICU 77) to `2031 a las 5:06:07` (ICU 78), and that is what reddened `Test Core (6/8)` on the reviewed head. On this head: (a) `auth-templates-locales.test.ts` pins the sentence FRAME per locale literally and computes the instant with `Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { dateStyle: 'long', timeStyle: 'long', timeZone })`, the same options the formula `datetime` formatter uses (packages/formula/src/template-engine.ts 106-116), then asserts the instant carries the year and the zone name and that `frame + instant + frame` appears in both faces; a template that used `date:long`, `datetime:medium` or the wrong locale or zone would still fail, so what the pin proves (the row renders exactly that instant, in the row's locale and the send's zone, inside that sentence) is unchanged. The Asia/Shanghai case now asserts the Shanghai rendering differs from the UTC one, carries `13:06:07`, and is what the zh-CN body prints. (b) `builtin-auth-render-identity.test.ts` cuts the formatted instant out of each face by literal `split` and digests the remainder with a `{{EXPIRES_AT_LONG}}` marker in its place; it additionally asserts the instant occurs exactly once in each `auth.invitation` face and zero times in every other row's faces, so every byte except the locale-data wording stays pinned and the position of the hole is pinned too. That is not weaker than the old digest; it is the same digest with one ICU-owned span held out, plus a presence-and-count assertion the old pin did not make. The digests themselves moved only for the four invitation rows. (c) `plain-text-faces.test.ts` replaces the `\s`-tolerant regex with exact equality against this Node's own `Intl` rendering plus the full stop, which is stronger. One honest limit, not a weakening: the frame tests now mirror the formatter's `Intl` options rather than an independent literal, so a regression that changed the formula formatter and the test together would pass; the formatter is not in this diff and the dogfood gate exercises it elsewhere.
10. **Timezone.** The invitation send passes no `timezone`, so the wall-clock renders in the server's zone; the `long` style names the zone, so the sentence is unambiguous. Acceptable, and the dev names it as a separate change.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset `.changeset/25802-invitation-role-label-warn-and-expiry.md` is byte-identical to the reviewed head. It bumps `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/plugin-email` at `patch`, with a `fix(...)!:` title, a BREAKING banner carrying Before, Now and a one-line Fix, a `Clause-②:` line and a `Metadata-protocol:` line. The two packages are exactly the two whose published behaviour moves (the warn in plugin-auth, the rows in plugin-email).
- The PR body's `Clause-②:` line reads `no (narrowing: the built-in auth.invitation rows declare a new required variable, expiresAt, so a sendTemplate of auth.invitation that names no expiresAt is now refused with MISSING_VARIABLES where it used to be sent)` and is identical to the changeset's line; the body is unchanged since the reviewed head. Check Changeset on this head is `success`; on the reviewed head its readings were `declaration line` declared, `direction arm: narrowing`, `metadata-protocol: none`, and the level axis accepts `patch` for a non-protocol change under the re-ruled decoupling. Nothing it reads moved. The Clause-② line matches what the diff publishes.
- `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right on the facts in ① items 3 to 5: no authorable key, spelling or stored shape moves, the email-template schema is unchanged, and the repair is a value only a sender holds, which no ledger entry can derive. `check-adr-0087-registration` accepts it (`[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)`); the Before/Now/Fix block is a code-side instruction, not a FROM-to-TO metadata rewrite, so the prescription detector is right not to refuse it.
- The dogfood battery the `(narrowing)` arm owes: the PR body reports it at the reviewed head (296 files passed, 3 skipped; 2523 tests passed, 18 skipped; exit 0), no non-test byte moved since, and the CI `Dogfood Regression Gate` on this head is `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Check-runs on this head (read 2026-10-26T12:30Z): 36 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure, 0 pending.** Build Core, Lint and Repo Gates (all sub-jobs), TypeScript Type Check, Type Check workspace/consumer/debt/source, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test Core and all eight shards, the four card/branch claim checks, Check PR Size, Flag docs, Auto Label: `success`. The skipped runs are the opt-in and UI-only families this diff does not reach. The red `Test Core (6/8)` of the reviewed head is green here; the one commit between the heads is the test-only ICU pin fix judged in ① item 9.
- `open_questions`: `[]` in both os-dev-reports. Nothing to answer. No card or PR comment was added after the second os-dev-report; the PR carries one bot comment (docs-drift check) naming three hand-written docs that mention the literal `expiresAt`, which is a documentation-accuracy re-verification for the docs seat, not a contract matter.
- Dev flag, cloud half: the measured remaining cause of the `Member` label is the cloud control plane's i18n composition (a declared `supportedLocales` that does not name `zh-CN`, or bundle registration). Routed to seat 2 by the dev, outside this repository; this PR adds the warn that names that check. Escalated to the seat as the card's second half; the card does not close on this PR alone until that half is read.
- Dev flag, unfiled observation: `FileI18nAdapter.getTranslations('zh')` answers `{}` on exact-key match while the kernel memory provider resolves `zh` to `zh-CN`, so one `supportedLocales` declaration translates on one provider and not the other. Composed-kernel probe only, no public-door reach; the dev left it unfiled per the report contract. The seat decides whether to file; it is the shape the new warn's text already points at (`zh-CN, not zh`).
- Dev flag, follow-up: `auth.password_reset`, `auth.magic_link` and `auth.two_factor_otp` declare `expiresInMinutes` `required: false` and print `expires in {{expiresInMinutes}} minutes` unconditionally, the same dangle this PR closes for the invitation. Not this card; a follow-up card is the right carrier.
- Dev flag, timezone: no reference timezone is passed on the invitation send (see ① item 10). Acceptable; a separate change if wanted.
- Claim boundary: the claim forbade `packages/spec/**`; the diff touches none. The claim's `Clause-②: no (expected; additive)` was superseded by the dev's measurement to `no (narrowing)` in the patch round, which is the right direction of correction.
- `#24154` stays closed: its ruling (the role in a Chinese invitation reads 成员) is what the label read delivers when the bundles reach it; this PR makes the residual miss loud rather than reopening it.
